description: A bakery makes fiber supplemented brownies and lemon squares. Each brownie requires 5 units of chocolate mix and 4 units of fiber. Each lemon square requires 7 units of lemon mix and 6 units of fiber. Lemon squares sell much faster and thus the number of lemon squares made must be larger than the number of brownies made. However, to please all customers, at least 40% of the items made must be brownies. If the bakery has 2500 units of chocolate mix and 3300 units of lemon mix, how many of each should be made to minimize the total amount of fiber needed?

ChocolateMixPerBrownie.definition: Amount of chocolate mix required to produce one brownie

FiberPerBrownie.definition: Amount of fiber required to produce one brownie

LemonMixPerLemonSquare.definition: Amount of lemon mix required to produce one lemon square

FiberPerLemonSquare.definition: Amount of fiber required to produce one lemon square

TotalChocolateMix.definition: Total units of chocolate mix available

TotalLemonMix.definition: Total units of lemon mix available

MinBrowniePercentage.definition: Minimum percentage of items that must be brownies

MinLemonExceedsBrownie.definition: Minimum required difference between the number of lemon squares and brownies

objective.description: "Minimize the total amount of fiber required to produce the brownies and lemon squares"
